answer: A stake-weighted reputation registry makes each identity pay to exist: an agent locks a deposit before it can trade, and misbehavior slashes it. Climbing that ridge of trust takes repeated honest work, so one attacker cannot cheaply spawn a thousand sock puppets, since the cost multiplies with every fake. Like a crystal, the record is transparent and hard to forge, so peers verify history instead of trusting claims. Even at the zenith of scale the economics hold: fakes stay unprofitable while real agents keep their stake.
